definition: U-Net is a convolutional neural network that was developed for image segmentation.
details: The network is based on a fully convolutional neural network whose architecture was modified and extended to work with fewer training images and to yield more precise segmentation. Segmentation of a 512 × 512 image takes less than a second on a modern (2015) GPU using the U-Net architecture. The U-Net architecture has also been employed in diffusion models for iterative image denoising. This technology underlies many modern image generation models, such as DALL-E, Midjourney, and Stable Diffusion. U-Net is also being explored for language models. Tokenization is not a separate step, allowing the model to more easily understand spelling and concurrently vectorizing / tokenizing higher level concepts.

explainer.lead: U-Net is a convolutional neural network built for image segmentation, notable for working with fewer training images while producing more precise segmentation. It also underlies many modern image generation models.

tiers.eli5: Like tracing the exact outline of every object in a photo, and getting it done so fast you hardly notice the wait.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use U-Net when labelled images are scarce but pixel-accurate masks are needed; a pitfall is trusting precision on domains far from the training images.

explainer.example: Segmenting a 512 × 512 medical scan into regions takes less than a second on a modern 2015 GPU with U-Net.
